name: The Great Wall (Jinshanling section)
scaleNote: 0.6 studs per metre over 400 m of the cited Jinshanling profile. At 1 stud/m the same stretch was 9 168 placements.

height.source: Wikipedia, Great Wall of China: at Juyong Pass the wall is '7.8 m (25 ft 7 in) high and 5 m (16 ft 5 in) wide'. At Jinshanling it 'ranges from 5 to 8 m (16 ft 3 in to 26 ft 3 in) in height'.

baseWidth.source: Wikipedia, Great Wall of China: at Jinshanling '6 m (19 ft 8 in) across the bottom, narrowing up to 5 m (16 ft 5 in) across the top'.

topWidth.source: Wikipedia, Great Wall of China: at Jinshanling '6 m (19 ft 8 in) across the bottom, narrowing up to 5 m (16 ft 5 in) across the top'.

note:
A SECTION, NOT THE WALL. The Ming wall is 8 850 km long; no scale renders that and no frame holds it. What this Atlas builds is 400 m of the cited Jinshanling profile with three watchtowers, and says so in its own title. Anything else would be a claim the model does not support.

The watchtower dimensions and spacing are uncited: the source read gives an estimated 25 000 watchtowers and no typical height or interval.

The towers stand BEHIND the wall rather than inside it. A real Ming watchtower straddles the rampart; two bricks cannot share a cubic millimetre, so the model abuts them at the wall's cited 6 m base width.
